text: The Beginner project at Thornbury Cycle Supply Co. solved one problem for one person. This project starts the moment that assumption breaks, with two stakeholders asking for a report in the same week.

The Marketing Manager wants the sales mix between Individual customers and Store slash Reseller customers. The Sales Director wants a territory benchmark, showing how each territory compares to the company as a whole.

Individual versus Store slash Reseller isn't an invented marketing segment. It's a real distinction already in the Sales dot Customer table: a row has either PersonID populated, for an individual, or StoreID populated, for a reseller, never both.

Two different people pull two different T-SQL extracts, one customer-focused, one territory-focused. Each looks fine alone, but combining them surfaces duplicate rows and inconsistent values, so this project builds a real pipeline: T-SQL extract, then Python cleaning and joining, then Power BI modeling and reporting.
Next lesson lays that pipeline out in plain English, stage by stage, before any code gets written.
